title: The Cognitive Neuroscience of Nature?: Sociological and Historical Perspective on Environmental Neuroscience

findings.consequent: Measurable change to the brain
findings.quote: new research that showed how, beyond even the everyday pleasure and invigoration of outdoor exercise, “staying home is just plain dumb.” Under the title, Hiking Makes You Smarter, the journalist, Elisabeth Kwak-Hefferan, described how she had recently taken part in a pilot study in a Utah canyon, to show how being exposed to nature can cause a measurable change to the brain.

findings.consequent: Think and focus more acutely, destress, calm down, happier
findings.quote: being out in the wilderness would make a person think and focus more acutely; it would destress them, calm them down, make them measurably happier.

findings.consequent: Prefrontal cortex over-burdened, over-worked, tired, stressed out
findings.quote: the prefrontal cortex, an area of the brain that was becoming chronically over-burdened by the “buzzers, sirens, and ringtones of life”—that was now increasingly over-worked, tired, stressed out.

findings.consequent: Good for minds, improved mental health, capacity to think clearly
findings.quote: the mere idea itself, that nature contact is good for our minds, that it improves our mental health and our capacity to think clearly, all of this is, somehow, something we already know intuitively—we know it already because we can feel it

findings.antecedent: Social and historical context (urbanization, place of nature, modern built environment catastrophe)
findings.consequent: Emergence of environmental neuroscience
findings.quote: environmental neuroscience has emerged within a very specific social and historical context. Understanding the field as a social phenomenon, I suggest, means understanding how it is embedded in, and reproductive of, a set of historical trajectories and macro-social contexts—about urbanization, about the place of nature, and about the perceived catastrophe of our modern built environment.

findings.consequent: Brain function
findings.quote: we might also read environmental neuroscience as simply one part of a wider realization, common to a larger set of neuro-disciplines, that the environment has a much larger role in brain function than was previously thought.

findings.consequent: Understanding behavior
findings.quote: simply controlling for, or regressing out, environmental context is not sufficient to truly understand behavior

findings.consequent: Brain phenotype variance
findings.quote: if genome-wide association studies explain only a small portion of brain phenotype variance—then environment, or environmental exposure, must explain the remainder

findings.consequent: Conceptual grounding of environmental neuroscience
findings.quote: the role of the physical environment is exclusively established as the conceptual grounding of the field.

findings.antecedent: Natural environment (vegetation, greenery, distance from urban centers, absence of humans)
findings.consequent: Soothes and calms mind, protects from urban stress
findings.quote: there is a growing consensus, within environmental neuroscience, that there is something about the physical parameters of nature, some perhaps still not fully understood visual, olfactory, or atmospheric quality of natural materials or scenes, that soothes and calms the mind—a quality that protects the modern person, and in particular, the modern urban person, from the stresses and strains of life in the city

findings.consequent: Cognitive load of urban space
findings.quote: specifically modern architecture and planning worsen the cognitive load of urban space.

findings.consequent: Mental health problems
findings.quote: urbanization is “one of the most important global health issues of the twenty-first century, in particular since mental health problems seem to be more frequent in cities… to safeguard mental and physical well-being in cities, research is needed that is targeted at identifying salutogenic factors of living environments”

findings.consequent: Mental health problems (schizophrenia, affective and anxiety disorders, autism)
findings.quote: mental health problems typically accumulate in urban areas. This seems to be especially true for schizophrenia, affective and anxiety disorders and autism.

findings.consequent: Knowledge base for evidence-based urban landscape planning
findings.quote: we anticipate that the research field of environmental neuroscience may in the long run provide a knowledge base for evidence-based urban landscape planning

findings.consequent: Psychological effects (anger, aggression, PTSD, depression, stress, burnout)
findings.quote: climate breakdown has quite direct psychological effects: heat increases the likelihood of anger and aggression; being caught in a major environmental disaster is likely to produce PTSD and depression; people displaced by climate events will experience stress and burnout

findings.antecedent: Climate breakdown (indirect effects, e.g., climate anxiety, solastalgia)
findings.consequent: Mental illness, threatened mental wellbeing
findings.quote: climate anxiety, climate grief, ecological trauma, or sometimes, using Glenn Albrecht’s and his collaborators’ terms, “solastalgia” and “psychoterratic illnesses”... describes an “earth-related mental illness where people’s mental wellbeing (psyche) is threatened by the severing of healthy links between themselves and their home/territory.”

findings.consequent: Overcoming political interest, right course of action, competing interests fall away
findings.quote: There is sometimes a sense in the concluding sections of environmental neuroscience papers that biological data will simply overcome political interest—that if the right people simply pay attention to the science, then the right course of action will follow, and competing interests will fall away.

findings.consequent: Affirmative activity
findings.quote: architectural shaping is not an obviously affirmative activity.

findings.antecedent: Healthier, restful, calmer working environments (via environmental neuroscience)
findings.consequent: Economically efficient spaces, extract value from employee with less friction
findings.quote: making working environments that are healthier, more restful, calmer, also means making spaces that are more economically efficient, that extract value from the employee with less visible friction.

findings.consequent: Ideological position associated with reactionary political actors
findings.quote: a preference for traditional design is an ideological position often associated with very reactionary political actors.
